question: Should explicit requester consumption of descendant output count as terminal delivery proof even when the requester's final outward send later fails?
rationale: The patch can implement either rule correctly, but the choice determines whether cleanup suppresses future delivery attempts and therefore requires an owner-approved product invariant rather than automation judgment.

options.title: Consumption is terminal proof
options.body: Treat explicit requester consumption as delivered, then merge only after exact-head restart proof and removal of unrelated refactors.

options.title: Require outward delivery
options.body: Keep descendants pending until the requester's composed result is visibly delivered, preserving retries when the final send fails.

options.title: Fold into durable inbox
options.body: Pause this branch and resolve the accounting rule as part of the broader durable completion inbox tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/67777.

recommendation.title: Consumption is terminal proof
recommendation.body: Treat explicit requester consumption as delivered, then merge only after exact-head restart proof and removal of unrelated refactors.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest recent ownership signal is on the cron fallback and adjacent subagent lifecycle implementation that defines when descendant output is adopted.
